bug_semantics: sch_teql keeps a circular singly linked list of slave qdiscs in teql_master->slaves / teql_sched_data->next. teql_qdisc_init() inserts, teql_destroy() unlinks, teql_master_xmit() rotates the head after a successful slave xmit or neighbour resolve, and teql_dequeue() also rewrites the head, all as plain pointer stores with no list lock and no RCU accessors. Concurrent RTM_NEWQDISC/RTM_DELQDISC on slaves (CAP_NET_ADMIN, including a user/netns) races with teql0 transmit: teql_destroy() can unlink a Qdisc that teql_master_xmit() still holds, the object is then freed after the qdisc RCU grace period, and the xmit walk (not in an RCU-bh read-side section covering that list) dereferences the stale pointer. KASAN: slab-use-after-free read of size 8 in teql_master_xmit of a freed kmalloc-512 qdisc. Attack path is local rtnetlink qdisc churn plus packet injection through teql0.
flaw_origin: The lockless circular slaves list and the four mutation sites were first written in net/sched/sch_teql.c at the public git root 1da177e4c3f41524e886b7f1b8a0c1fc7321cac2 (Linux-2.6.12-rc2 import, Alexey Kuznetsov teql). Later commits only restyled, converted netdev/qdisc APIs, or fixed unrelated teql bugs (noop_qdisc OOPS, NULL master in destroy, lockless qdisc_reset double-free); none added a list lock or RCU protection. The 2018 qdisc RCU-free path made the use-after-free show up as a post-grace-period slab UAF but did not first write the missing synchronization.
